verdict: Caution: lend selectively in Neemrana auto components to tier-1/tier-2 suppliers with OEM-backed order books and tight covenants; avoid single-OEM, EV-powertrain-exposed and thin-margin job-work units until local demand signals improve.
title: Neemrana Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**An auto-component plant in Neemrana takes steel, aluminium, plastic and electronics, stamps or moulds them into parts, and sells them to OEMs on annual price-down contracts.** Cash is made on volume and tooling, not price: OEMs demand a yearly cost reduction, so margin comes from utilisation and yield. Working capital sits in receivables from OEMs and in inventory of metals; capex is press/mould lines and tooling. **So when a proposal lands, check the OEM contract tenure and the annual price-down clause first; if the buyer is a single OEM, ask for the second customer pipeline.**

## What has changed now
**The national picture is strong but the local one is not.** India-wide auto-component output (NIC 29) is up 25.2% YoY and 19.2% Apr-to-date [D], and peers confirm demand: Motherson Sumi Wiring profit up 35% to Rs 223 crore with revenue up 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore [4], Lumax lifted its growth outlook [7]. **But Rajasthan GST collections are -4.7% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and electricity demand +4.0% against India +9.5% [D] — the state is running 10.8 pp and 5.5 pp behind the country.** Treat that as a local demand and cash-cycle warning, not a national one.

## Where the growth is
**Neemrana has real anchor investment: Toyoda Gosei's airbag plant [2] and Tokai Rika Minda's smart keys, shift levers and seat belts plant at 384,022 units per month [3].** Both are 2024 news, so verify current utilisation with the customer. **Pursue tier-2 suppliers feeding these anchors — wiring, plastics, stamping, seat-belt and airbag sub-assemblies — with purchase orders from more than one tier-1.** Avoid pure job-work units and engine/diesel-part makers: rating commentary flags higher obsolescence risk for engine-related parts as EVs spread [11].

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the P&L.** Rating commentary notes gross current assets averaging 160-170 days [10], so size the drawing power on that cycle and take monthly stock and debtor statements. **Covenant Debt/EBITDA below 2.5-2.75 times [10] and a minimum 1.2x current ratio; if the proposal breaches either, ask for promoter infusion before sanction.** Take monthly GST returns, quarterly OEM order books and a half-yearly stock audit.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the local signals, not the national headline.** If Rajasthan GST stays negative for another quarter [D], tighten new sanctions. If a borrower's electricity bill or power-factor reading falls, that is falling utilisation — ask for the production log. **If a borrower's OEM price-down exceeds the metal-cost pass-through, margin is being squeezed; ask for the revised costing sheet.** Rating reports here are undated, so treat them as methodology, not current fact.
